What it replaces

Window manager. Launcher. Clipboard manager. Screenshot tool. Dictation app. Drop-down terminal. Web-app wrapper. AI chat. Pilot.

One native app, written in Swift, on one key and one look. Nothing to subscribe to, no tracking, and the speech and file search run on your Mac.

First open

You need macOS 27 or later on a Mac with Apple silicon.

  1. Download Pilot.dmg with the Download button, open it and drag Pilot to Applications.
  2. Open Pilot. macOS says Apple could not verify it, because Pilot is open source and not notarized. Click Done.
  3. Within the hour, open System Settings › Privacy & Security. Scroll to Security, click Open Anyway beside Pilot, then enter your login password.
  4. Pilot opens its setup. Pick your layer key (Caps Lock is suggested: tapped alone it is Escape, and Shift+Caps Lock still types capitals), then grant what it asks for:
    • Accessibility. Pilot needs it to see your keys and move windows; nothing works without it.
    • Full Disk Access if you want file search in the menu, and System Events for sleep, restart and dark mode.
    • The microphone for dictation and an AI provider for Quick AI, both optional.
    • Input Monitoring only if Pilot asks, when you bind a mouse's media buttons.
    • Screen Recording when you first take a screenshot or recording with Pilot, or turn on Menu bar › Other apps › Show exact menu bar items. macOS applies it after Pilot reopens: click Quit & Reopen.
  5. Updates install from inside Pilot. You won't see this warning again, and your permissions stay: every update is signed with the same certificate, so macOS knows it is the same app.

From Terminal instead of steps 2–3: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Pilot.app. Check the download against the .sha256 beside it on the Releases page: shasum -a 256 -c Pilot.dmg.sha256.

Hyper+Space opens the menu; its Learn › Keybindings lists every bind, and the Binds page in Pilot's window changes any of them. Password fields are blind to every key tap on macOS, Pilot's included: your binds do not work while one has focus.
